rows.selection_reason: With no prior evidence, the highest-value first experiment is to establish a simple, well-understood baseline. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the most minimal RNA-only configuration: it uses a standard linear dimensionality reduction (PCA to 2000 dims) and a single profile, avoiding confounds from learned encoders, multi-profile aggregation, or fusion. This gives a clean reference accuracy for RNA signal alone. In experiment 2 I can then test the image-only counterpart (e.g., config_010) to determine which modality carries more signal, and from there decide whether to invest remaining budget in multimodal fusion, better RNA encoders (scvi, scgpt), or multiprofile aggregation. Starting from the simplest baseline reduces uncertainty about the fundamental contribution of each modality before adding complexity.

Evidence: We have only one data point (config_001: RNA-only, single-profile, PCA → 48.5% acc). The most critical unknown is whether the image modality carries any predictive signal at all; without this, we cannot rationally decide whether to invest remaining budget in multimodal fusion. Question: config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) is the direct modality-counterpart to config_001, isolating the effect of switching from RNA to image features while keeping the profile setting (singleprofile) constant. This gives a clean, single-variable comparison. Why this is best: With 8 experiments left, establishing whether image features are informative is a prerequisite for any multimodal experiment to be worthwhile. If image accuracy is near chance, multimodal configs lose their rationale; if it is competitive or better, we gain a strong justification to explore fusion. Testing a different RNA encoder or multiprofile aggregation would be premature before we know whether the second modality is even useful.

Evidence: RNA-only with PCA n2000 (single profile) achieves 48.5% accuracy, while image-only with ResNet50 is very weak at 20.8%, establishing RNA as the dominant modality. Uncertainty: We don't yet know whether multiprofile representation with aggregation (avgpool) can improve upon the single-profile RNA baseline, and this is a foundational design choice that gates many downstream configurations. This experiment (config_002) is a minimal, clean extension of config_001—same encoder (PCA n2000), same modality (RNA), only adding multiprofile + avgpool—so it isolates the effect of multiprofile aggregation without confounding encoder or modality changes. If multiprofile helps, it validates a large family of configurations (transformer aggregation, other encoders, multimodal variants); if it doesn't, it efficiently prunes that branch and directs remaining budget toward encoder improvements or image modality exploration. With 7 experiments left, reducing uncertainty on this high-leverage design axis is the best use of the next slot.

Evidence: RNA multiprofile with pca_n2000 + avgpool (config_002) is the current best at 0.591 acc, a strong +10.6% improvement over singleprofile RNA (0.485), confirming multiprofile is the key design choice. Image-only is weak (0.208), so near-term gains likely come from refining the RNA pipeline. Uncertainty: We do not yet know whether transformer aggregation outperforms avgpool for multiprofile RNA, and this is a fundamental choice that will affect all future multiprofile and multimodal experiments. This experiment (config_003) tests exactly that: same model (rna_only), same profile (multiprofile), same encoder (pca_n2000), but transformer instead of avgpool. It is a clean single-variable comparison against config_002, isolating the aggregation effect. Under a 10-experiment budget with 6 remaining, establishing the best aggregation strategy now is critical before committing to multimodal fusion experiments, as it determines whether transformer-based aggregation is worth the added complexity in later configs.

Evidence: config_002 (RNA, multiprofile, PCA_n2000, avgpool) is the best at 0.591 acc, showing multiprofile+avgpool is the strongest RNA setup, while image alone is very weak (0.208). Uncertainty: whether a learned RNA encoder (scvi_n200) can capture non-linear biological structure that PCA misses, potentially improving on the current best. This experiment (config_005) isolates the encoder variable by swapping PCA_n2000 → scvi_n200 while keeping the proven multiprofile+avgpool setting, directly testing if a better representation lifts the best configuration. It is the best use of this slot because it builds on the strongest evidence, changes only one variable, and if successful establishes a stronger base for subsequent multimodal experiments within the remaining 5-experiment budget.

Evidence: config_005 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) is the current best at 0.6501 acc. We know multiprofile > singleprofile and avgpool > transformer, but we have not yet tested whether scgpt outperforms scvi_n200 as an RNA encoder under the best profile/aggregation settings. Question: Does scgpt provide a better cell representation than scvi_n200 when paired with multiprofile + avgpool? This is a clean single-variable comparison (encoder: scgpt vs scvi_n200) that isolates the representation choice. Why this experiment: It directly extends the best-known configuration to test the last unexplored RNA encoder, reducing uncertainty about whether we've found the optimal RNA representation. With 4 experiments remaining, confirming the best RNA-only baseline before exploring multimodal fusion is critical, as it determines whether adding image data is worth the remaining budget.

The current best is config_005 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) at 0.6501. The key open question is whether adding visual information can improve upon this, but the only prior image result (resnet50, singleprofile) was very weak (0.2079), leaving it unclear whether a stronger image encoder (ViT-L) would contribute meaningfully. Config_036 tests multimodal fusion using all the best-known RNA settings (scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool) combined with the strongest available image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) and simple concat fusion. This is the highest-information experiment: if it beats 0.6501, we unlock a promising multimodal direction for the remaining 3 experiments; if it does not, we confirm RNA-only is the ceiling and can spend remaining budget refining RNA-only configurations (e.g., transformer aggregation with scvi_n200). Using ViT-L rather than resnet50 is critical because resnet50's poor standalone performance may simply reflect a weak encoder, and testing multimodal with a known-weak image encoder would not resolve the core question.

The best result so far is config_036 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat) at 0.715 accuracy, showing a strong +0.065 gain over the best RNA-only model (config_005, 0.650). The fusion method (concat vs. weighted) is the only dimension of the best configuration that has not been explored, and there is no prior evidence favoring one over the other. config_037 changes only the fusion from concat to weighted, isolating that single variable. With only 2 experiments remaining after this one, testing the most uncertain design choice in the current best direction is the highest-value experiment: if weighted fusion improves accuracy, we gain a new best; if not, we can use the remaining budget to test another single-variable perturbation (e.g., aggregation) with confidence that fusion is settled.

The current best is config_036 (0.7150) using multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat. The only untested single-variable extension of this best configuration is swapping avgpool for transformer aggregation (config_038). While RNA-only evidence suggests avgpool outperforms transformer (0.5907 vs 0.5191 for pca_n2000), that comparison was made without image features in the pool. In the multimodal setting, the transformer may better model interactions between the richer set of profile tokens and the image representation, potentially pushing past 0.7150. This is a clean single-variable test that isolates the aggregation effect in the best-performing regime. With only 1 experiment remaining after this, the low risk (we retain config_036 if it underperforms) and the logical extension of the strongest evidence make this the best use of the 9th slot.

Evidence: The best-performing family is multimodal + multiprofile + scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l, with config_038 (transformer, concat) at 0.7207 as the current best. Within this family, transformer aggregation slightly outperforms avgpool (0.7207 vs 0.7150), and concat slightly outperforms weighted (0.7207 vs 0.7062). Question: config_039 (transformer + weighted) is the only untested combination in this top-performing family. It tests whether the interaction between transformer aggregation and weighted fusion could yield a different (potentially better) result than either component alone. Why: With 0 experiments remaining after this one, this is the only untested configuration in the family that has produced all results above 0.70. All other untested configurations involve inferior components (resnet50, PCA, scgpt, single-profile) that have consistently underperformed. While the marginal evidence suggests config_039 may not surpass config_038, it is the sole remaining opportunity to explore the full 2×2 aggregation×fusion space within the proven-best architecture, and any improvement would set the final best.
